concepts.title: What Is MCP
keyPoints: Open standard: JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol linking AI hosts to external tools/data
Solves the M×N integration problem — turns it into M+N
Host embeds one client per server (stdio or HTTP transport)
Servers expose tools (model-picks), resources (app-picks), prompts (user-picks)
Gotcha: standardizes wiring, not tool quality — vague schemas still hurt accuracy

concepts.title: Host, Client, and Server
keyPoints: Host = LLM-facing app (Claude Desktop/Code); owns conversation, UX, consent
Client = per-Server protocol object, not the LLM; 1:1 stateful JSON-RPC session
Server = isolated process (stdio local / HTTP remote) exposing tools/resources/prompts
Call flow: LLM picks tool → Host routes to owning Client → Client→Server via private transport → back up
Gotcha: only the Host sees across servers — isolation prevents one compromised server from touching another's credentials

concepts.title: Data and Transport Layers
keyPoints: Data layer: JSON-RPC 2.0 contract — requests, responses, notifications
Transport layer: stdio or Streamable HTTP — how bytes physically move
Same tool/resource/prompt code; transport is just a deploy-time switch
stdio gotcha: stdout is the wire — stray prints corrupt the stream
HTTP gotcha: pin sessions via Mcp-Session-Id or lose state on scale-out

concepts.title: JSON-RPC 2.0 Messaging
keyPoints: JSON-RPC 2.0 is MCP's wire format for every client↔server exchange
Three envelope types share "jsonrpc":"2.0" — request, response, notification
Notifications omit `id` and expect no reply (progress, cancelled, list_changed)
Each request `id` gets exactly one response: `result` or `error`, never both
Tool failures aren't JSON-RPC errors — return success with `isError:true` in result

concepts.title: Transports: stdio vs Streamable HTTP
keyPoints: Same JSON-RPC 2.0 data layer, different physical transport
stdio: client spawns server subprocess, pipes over stdin/stdout
stdio is 1:1 same-machine, no network/auth needed
Streamable HTTP: POST endpoint, optional SSE upgrade for streaming, session IDs via Mcp-Session-Id
Gotcha: stdio server must log to stderr, never stdout

concepts.title: Lifecycle and Capability Negotiation
keyPoints: Handshake: independently-versioned MCP client & server agree on version + capabilities
Phase 1: `initialize` request/response, then client sends `initialized` notification
Version negotiation = one round trip: client proposes newest, server counters
Capabilities nested: missing key = unsupported; empty object = base-only, no sub-features
Gotcha: don't call methods pre-`initialized` or via undeclared sub-capabilities

concepts.title: Security and Authorization
keyPoints: HTTP transport = OAuth 2.1 resource server; stdio = OS process boundary, no handshake
401 + WWW-Authenticate points client to Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728)
Client then runs Authorization Code + PKCE, token audienced to this MCP server (RFC 8707)
Server must validate `aud` claim on every request, not just signature/expiry
Token passthrough (forwarding an unaudienced bearer token) = confused-deputy vulnerability

concepts.title: Notifications
keyPoints: JSON-RPC message with `method`, no `id`, no response
Either client or server can send a notification
Types: progress, logging (`notifications/message`), `list_changed`, `resources/updated`
Change/log notifications require prior capability negotiation (e.g. `listChanged`)
Best-effort only — no ack, no retries, delivery not guaranteed

concepts.title: Prompts
keyPoints: Named server-defined message template, selected explicitly by the user, not the model
Discovered via prompts/list, rendered to chat messages via prompts/get
Server returns finished role/content messages, spliced straight into the conversation
Can seed multi-turn scaffolds — one call returns several messages (e.g. user + canned assistant reply)
Gotcha: arguments are untyped strings (no inputSchema) and the model can never auto-invoke prompts/get

concepts.title: Resources
keyPoints: Read-only, URI-addressable data (file/record/log/schema) via resources/read
Application-controlled — host decides what to attach, not the model
Static via resources/list; parameterized via resources/templates/list (RFC 6570)
Read returns text OR blob (base64, ~33% size tax), never both
Model can't pull resources itself — needs a Tool wrapping the fetch

concepts.title: Roots and Logging
keyPoints: Roots: client-advertised file:// URIs marking directories a server may operate in
Server calls roots/list; re-lists on notifications/roots/list_changed as workspace changes
Logging: client sets minimum severity via logging/setLevel (RFC 5424: debug→emergency)
Server emits notifications/message at/above that level instead of stdout prints
Gotcha: roots are advisory only — server must independently validate/prefix-check every path

concepts.title: Tools
keyPoints: Named, JSON-Schema-typed function: listed via tools/list, executed via tools/call
Model-controlled — LLM itself decides when to call it, picks arguments
Round trip: tools/list → model emits args → tools/call → {content, isError?}
Domain failure → isError:true (retryable); malformed call → JSON-RPC protocol error
Tool text is untrusted — enables poisoning/rug-pulls; confirm destructive actions with humans

concepts.title: Building an MCP Server
keyPoints: Thin JSON-RPC 2.0 shim exposing tools/resources/prompts — not a web app with routes
Initialize handshake: client/server exchange capabilities before any tool/resource call
FastMCP decorators infer JSON Schema from type hints; low-level Server API builds responses by hand
stdio gotcha: stdout is the wire — a stray print() breaks the client's parser
Tool failure ≠ protocol error: raise → FastMCP converts to CallToolResult{isError:true}, not a JSON-RPC error

concepts.title: MCP vs Alternatives
keyPoints: M×N tool integrations → M+N via one standard protocol (like LSP)
Client-server pair: JSON-RPC over stdio (local) or HTTP/SSE (remote)
Server exposes tools (actions), resources (read context), prompts (templates)
Still bottoms out in the same function-calling primitive underneath
Worth it once ≥2 consumers share a capability; else pure overhead

concepts.title: Sampling
keyPoints: Server-to-client request (`sampling/createMessage`) asking client to run an LLM completion
Reverses normal MCP direction — every other primitive is client-initiated
Client picks the model and holds credentials; server never sees an API key
Per spec, human reviews both the outgoing request and the returned completion
Optional capability negotiated at `initialize` — server must check and have a fallback

concepts.title: Elicitation
keyPoints: Server pauses mid-request, asks client's human for one fact via elicitation/create
Server sends message + flat JSON-schema; client renders a form
Client replies accept/decline/cancel plus data matching schema
Schema must be flat primitives only — no nested objects or arrays
Never elicit sensitive data (passwords, keys) — server could phish via trusted-looking form
